original_metadata.title: Positive non-acyclic Looijenga interiors over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero are exactly the finite-wrapping tropical surfaces with starred Kodaira inverse monodromy and the specified D/E blowup models
original_metadata.author: Travis Mandel
original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The classification ties the integral-linear developing map, regular-function valuations, boundary geometry and root lattice to a concrete rational-surface construction. The difficult converse must recover the toric blowup model from the minimal boundary data: the author uses pencils and a charge/Euler-characteristic contradiction to produce the needed exceptional curves, then inducts through the I_k^* family and reduces exceptional E cases using elliptic pencils. This supplies new geometric reconstruction rather than merely reading a Kodaira matrix from an existing model.

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: The full Theorem4.4 proof and essential local context were read: the integral-linear charts/developing map and line-wrap definitions, charge invariance, the prior theta-valuation background and negative/acyclic classifications, and the new positive non-acyclic boundary and surface classification. In particular the author supplies the nontrivial (5)->(6) construction: the cubic base case, pencil/Euler-characteristic argument forcing additional singular curves in the I_k^* cases, induction by non-toric blowdowns, and elliptic-pencil reductions for the exceptional cases. The listed similar III^*/II^* reductions specify their starting boundary and blowup construction. The effective lattice uses classes effective on some family fibre, not on every fixed generic surface. No finite-type neighbour or strong-deformation theorem is counted separately.

original_metadata.statement_scope: Exactly all seven equivalent conditions of Theorem4.4 for a Looijenga interior U=Y minus D over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic zero, with Y smooth projective rational and D a reduced nodal anticanonical cycle. Positivity and non-acyclicity use the paper conventions. Every tropical line wraps finitely and nonzero times; equivalently the inverse monodromy is conjugate to starred Kodaira I_k^*, IV^*, III^* or II^*. The explicit P^2 triangle non-toric blowup multiplicities are (2,2,2+k), (2,3,3), (2,3,4), (2,3,5), with the precise boundary, valuation, developing-map and D_n/E_n lattice conditions of the theorem retained. The lattice D_Eff^perp is generated by classes effective on some fibre, as defined on physical p.10. The reconstruction concerns the prescribed deformation/fibrewise classification and chosen blowup points, not unique isomorphism of every surface or the stronger decorated deformation statement5.8.
original_metadata.editorial_warning: The monodromy appearing in the selected classification is the inverse mu^{-1}; replacing it by mu changes the listed matrices. The effective-lattice condition refers to effectiveness on some fibre, and not to existence of all these curves on a generic fixed U. The phrase “as in Table4.1” includes its full multiplicity table on physical p.23. The short source transition “similar” in the III^*/II^* elliptic-pencil reductions is retained with the explicit boundary and blowup prescriptions supplied by the author.
original_metadata.source_boundary_note: The complete original seven-condition Theorem 4.4 and author proof are retained with tropical charts/developing map, inverse-monodromy changes, charge, positivity and valuation background and the full starred-Kodaira multiplicity table. The new boundary/surface classification includes the cubic base case, pencil/Euler-characteristic contradiction, non-toric-blowdown induction and elliptic-pencil reductions. Neighboring negative/acyclic classifications are retained as uncounted context because the author uses them in the selected lattice exclusion step. The effective lattice means classes effective on some family fibre; no fixed generic-surface or unique-isomorphism assertion is added.
